Hi Vivek,

We're close to kick-off for a small pilot at Acme (payments team). Procurement asked whether we can go through AWS Marketplace (they prefer single-invoice/marketplace SaaS) or if we should execute a direct Redwood MSA + PO. I've attached our standard procurement questionnaire (Acme_procurement_qs.pdf). Can you advise on the tradeoffs from Redwood's perspective and any paperwork timeline differences? Also copying our cloud procurement contact (they asked me to loop Redwood sales).

Samantha — thanks for the clear note and the questionnaire. Quick summary up front, then suggested next steps.

Short summary (tradeoffs):
- Marketplace (AWS/Azure/GCP): fastest procurement for customers who require marketplace billing; supports private offers and consolidated invoicing, typically faster PO approval. However, marketplace T&Cs can limit custom contract language (indemnities, audit clauses, data residency addenda), and co-sell incentives depend on whether Acme uses the AWS co-sell program and whether we register the deal.
- Direct contract (Redwood MSA + PO): gives full control over SLAs, data controls, and standard enterprise terms. Longer legal review but better for multiyear commitments, custom SOWs, and guaranteed SLA credits.

Practical recommendation for Acme pilot: pursue a Marketplace private offer to unblock immediate pilot (start-by-Oct-1) while parallel-tracking a direct MSA for enterprise commit post-pilot. That gives speed now, control later.

Next steps I propose:
1) Quick 30-min sync (we can include our marketplace contact and your procurement).
2) We'll draft a marketplace private offer and share pricing (I attached a two-slide matrix).
3) Laura will flag any non-negotiable legal items you call out so we know whether the marketplace route will be a blocker.

I've attached a short internal matrix that maps decision criteria to recommended routes (routing_quick_matrix.pdf). Marcus will add notes about integration/support differences.

Best,
Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

Adding a tech/ops lens — quick points to consider for Acme's decision: 
- Observability & support: with a marketplace private offer the routing and billing are through AWS but runtime and support remain Redwood; we need to ensure the support SLA and escalation paths are documented in the private offer or an attached SOW.
- Data residency/hosting: Marketplace listings can support region constraints, but for on-prem or VPC-private deployments we'll need a direct order (private deployment addendum). If Acme needs specific VPC peering or dedicated nodes, that pushes to direct.
- Integrations and metrics: If Acme wants to instrument per-token cost and latency metrics into their internal dashboards (trace/route hooks), we should include that in the SOW for direct deals. For a short pilot we can provide limited telemetry via existing APIs.

Operational timeline: marketplace private offer + listing sign-off: ~1-2 weeks to create offer + customer acceptance. Direct MSA + negotiated SOW: typically 3–6 weeks (depends on legal).

Happy to run the 30-min technical portion on Monday.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference

Hi all — jumping in from AWS Marketplace to clarify a few common points that come up for customers like Acme: 
- Billing cadence: marketplace invoices are issued monthly by AWS to the customer, and AWS pays the ISV on a 30–60 day schedule depending on settlement terms. If Acme requires vendor invoicing terms (Net 30 to Redwood), a private offer can be negotiated to align with that, though the invoicing party remains AWS unless you opt for vendor-billed offers.
- Co-sell incentives: for accounts that participate in AWS co-sell, registering the opportunity and co-selling through the AM can yield incentives for both the AM and our partner. We can help register the opportunity once Redwood confirms the deal registration.
- Custom terms & addenda: Marketplace supports private offers with attached SOWs. However, marketplace T&Cs are standard; any negotiable items should be surfaced in the private offer process early so we can determine if they require a direct contract.

If useful, I can run a quick call with Acme procurement and Redwood to explain private offer flows and expected timelines.

Best,
Tom Price
AWS Marketplace Sales
aws-marketplace-sales@amazon.com

Samantha / Vivek — quick legal note:
- Marketplace T&Cs are generally non-negotiable on core terms (liability caps, indemnities). If Acme has strict audit or data processing addendum requirements we should surface them now; sometimes those can be attached as an addendum to a private offer but often they require a separate MSA addendum.
- If Acme requires a custom SLA with financial credits, direct MSA is the safer route. We can draft a short pilot SOW with limited SLA commitments that can ride on a private offer as long as Acme accepts the SOW language.

I'll prepare a short redline checklist for marketplace vs direct and share by EOD.

Laura Bennett
Head of Legal, Redwood Inference
